title: GCAM and integrated assessment emulators
summary: Integrated assessment models such as GCAM link energy, land, water, economy and climate, but each run is slow. Emulators trained on a few runs make thousands of policy scenarios and uncertainty studies possible.
outcomes: describe what GCAM represents and why its runs are expensive
build a Gaussian process emulator of a GCAM-like transport output
use emulator uncertainty to choose the next full-model run (active learning)
discuss the limits of emulators for policy analysis
narration_en: Integrated assessment models, or IAMs, such as GCAM, the Global Change Analysis Model developed at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, represent how energy, agriculture and land, water, the economy and the climate interact across the world's regions until the end of the century. They answer questions such as: what carbon price would cut transport emissions by half by 2050, and what would it do to electricity demand and land use? Each scenario can take hours to run, yet policy questions need thousands of runs to explore combinations of carbon prices, technology costs and behaviour, and to quantify uncertainty. Emulators make this feasible. We run GCAM at a carefully chosen set of inputs, train a fast statistical model, often a Gaussian process, on the outputs, and use it for everything else. The emulator's uncertainty tells us where it is unsure, so we run GCAM next exactly there: this is active learning. In our toy example, five well-placed runs already give an emulator error near one percent. In this module you will decide how many runs to buy, and where.
narration_ar: تمثّل نماذج التقييم المتكامل، مثل GCAM، أي نموذج تحليل التغير العالمي الذي طوّره مختبر شمال غرب المحيط الهادئ الوطني، كيفية تفاعل الطاقة والزراعة واستخدام الأراضي والمياه والاقتصاد والمناخ عبر أقاليم العالم حتى نهاية القرن. وهي تجيب عن أسئلة مثل: ما سعر الكربون الذي يخفض انبعاثات النقل إلى النصف بحلول عام 2050، وما أثره في الطلب على الكهرباء واستخدام الأراضي؟ وقد يستغرق تشغيل السيناريو الواحد ساعات، بينما تحتاج أسئلة السياسات إلى آلاف التشغيلات لاستكشاف تركيبات أسعار الكربون وتكاليف التقنيات والسلوك، ولتقدير عدم اليقين. والمحاكيات تجعل هذا ممكناً: نشغّل GCAM عند مجموعة مدخلات مختارة بعناية، وندرّب نموذجاً إحصائياً سريعاً، غالباً عملية غاوسية، على مخرجاته، ونستخدمه لكل ما عدا ذلك. ويخبرنا عدم يقين المحاكي أين يكون غير متأكد، فنشغّل GCAM بعد ذلك هناك تحديداً، وهذا هو التعلم النشط. وفي مثالنا التعليمي تعطي خمسة تشغيلات موزعة جيداً محاكياً بخطأ يقارب واحداً بالمئة. ستقرر في هذه الوحدة كم تشغيلاً ستشتري، وأين.

tour.text: GCAM couples energy, land, water, economy and climate, but runs slowly.
Run it at a few carefully chosen inputs.
Train a fast emulator on the results.

sections.heading: What GCAM represents
sections.html: GCAM (Calvin et al. 2019) is an open-source integrated assessment model with 32 energy-economy regions, hundreds of land and water units, and detailed technology choices in buildings, industry and transport. Markets clear every five years; emissions feed a simple climate model. Its transport sector represents passenger and freight modes and vehicle technologies, competing on cost through logit choice. Because everything is linked, a carbon price changes vehicle choices, electricity generation and land use at once.

sections.heading: Building the emulator
sections.html: Pick an output, here transport CO₂ in 2050 versus carbon price. Run the full model at a few prices, fit a Gaussian process (module 2.6) and check it on extra runs. In the explorer: 3 evenly spread runs give an error of about 0.08 Gt; 5 runs about 0.013 Gt (around 1%); 5 runs bunched at low prices about 0.2 Gt, because the high-price region is unexplored.

sections.heading: Active learning
sections.html: Start with three runs, then repeatedly run the full model where the emulator's uncertainty is largest. In the lab the error falls from 0.085 Gt (3 runs) to about 0.01 Gt (7 runs), with each new run placed automatically in the least-known region. With many inputs (carbon price, battery cost, biofuel availability, behaviour), space-filling designs and dimension reduction are needed first.

sections.heading: Limits and good practice
sections.html: An emulator is only as good as the model it copies: it inherits GCAM's assumptions and cannot correct structural errors. It is valid only inside the sampled input ranges. Multi-output emulators must keep physical consistency (shares summing to one, emissions consistent with energy). Report emulator uncertainty alongside model uncertainty, and validate on held-out full runs. Published GCAM emulators and 'fast IAM' surrogates are an active research area.

code.title: A GP emulator with active learning
code.explain: Start with three runs; add each new run where the emulator is most uncertain.
code.expected:
3 runs: emulator error 0.0845 Gt, largest uncertainty at 300 $/t
4 runs: emulator error 0.0768 Gt, largest uncertainty at 95 $/t
5 runs: emulator error 0.0125 Gt, largest uncertainty at 354 $/t
6 runs: emulator error 0.0126 Gt, largest uncertainty at 43 $/t
7 runs: emulator error 0.0104 Gt, largest uncertainty at 152 $/t

takeaways: GCAM links energy, land, water, economy and climate across regions, but runs are slow.
A Gaussian process emulator trained on a few runs answers thousands of policy questions.
Active learning places new runs where the emulator is least certain.
Emulators inherit the model's assumptions and are valid only inside sampled ranges.
